main_dirt.bias_notes: Clockwise (Right-handed). Hokkaido's premier NAR venue featuring a wide 1,600m outer dirt oval and a generous 330m home straight. Unlike tight municipal tracks, Mombetsu's width and long straight afford a fair playing field where backmarkers and pressers can successfully overhaul early leaders.
main_dirt.post_bias: Fair barrier distribution across routes (1200m to 2000m). In 1000m sprint chutes, inside gates (1-4) hold a minor ground-saving edge before the bend, but wide runners are rarely penalized as severely as on tighter bullrings.

handicapping_angles.wide_track_fairness: Do not automatically default to extreme speed biases. Mombetsu's wide turns and 330m straight reward tactical pressers ('P') and balanced stalkers who time their run cleanly down the center.
handicapping_angles.hokkaido_sire_and_local_form: Hokkaido-bred juveniles (2yo) and local NAR runners acclimated to the cooler northern climate often show sharp improvement during the summer/autumn meet.
handicapping_angles.night_racing_moisture_shifts: During Grand Chariot Night meetings, dropping evening temperatures can seal the dirt surface, creating a subtle speed advantage as the card progresses.
handicapping_angles.jra_shipper_class_advantage: Class-dropping horses transitioning from JRA (Japan Racing Association) open company down to Mombetsu NAR local graded stakes carry a distinct class advantage.
